dedupe_keys.name: monthly crop water use for 26 crop types simulated with the global crop water model gcwm 1981 2021 siebert

description: Global monthly water use of 26 irrigated and rainfed crop types from 1981 to 2021, at 5 arc-minutes, simulated with the Global Crop Water Model (GCWM) and split into irrigation water (blue) and precipitation water stored in the soil (green), in cubic metres. The Zenodo record says GCWM runs a daily soil water balance per crop, with Penman-Monteith evapotranspiration after FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56, driven by ERA5 reanalysis downscaled from 15 to 5 arc-minutes with an elevation lapse rate of 0.65 K per 100 m, and crop areas and calendars from MIRCA2000, with sub-crops for multiple cropping and seasonal cereals. Version 1 was published on 4 December 2024 by Stefan Siebert as 28 downloadable ZIP files, one per crop plus grid cell area and a readme, about 41 GB in total, free under CC BY 4.0. Coverage is global cropland over 41 years. Caveats: crop areas are fixed at around 2000 from MIRCA2000, so changes in irrigated area are not reflected. For simulation it gives the monthly timing of irrigation demand, to test water supply, reservoir and pumping energy demand in dry seasons and droughts. Related catalogue records include MIRCA2000 monthly irrigated and rainfed crop areas and the ACEA water footprints of 175 crops.
